identity.name: House of Jagiellon
alt_names: Poland and Lithuania under the Jagiellons
Crown of Poland and Grand Duchy of Lithuania (1450-1569)

land.text: the Crown of Poland, in personal union with Lithuania under Casimir IV (King from 1447)

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's House of Jagiellon shape of 1450 (4,456 cells) is the union of its Kingdom of Poland and Grand Duchy of Lithuania shapes of 1449 (4,462 cells, 4,454 of them in common), both of which end in 1449.

land.text: the Grand Duchy, ruled by Casimir IV (Grand Duke since 1440)
the whole realm: the Union of Lublin of 1 July 1569 merges the Crown and the Grand Duchy into the Commonwealth

successors.note: Cliopatria's Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth row starts in 1572 and its House of Jagiellon row runs to 1571; the page dates the Commonwealth to 1569, so 1570-1571 belongs to the Commonwealth dossier.

capitals.name: Kraków
capitals.note: The Crown's capital: Kraków before 1596. Coordinates are not on the page.

capitals.name: Vilnius
capitals.note: The Grand Duchy's capital; the dynasty page says Sigismund II moved his court there in 1544. A second seat of the same realm, not a move.

rulers.name: Casimir IV Jagiellon
rulers.title: King of Poland (1447-1492) and Grand Duke of Lithuania (1440-1492)

rulers.name: John I Albert / Alexander
rulers.title: John I Albert King of Poland 1492-1501; Alexander Grand Duke of Lithuania 1492-1506
rulers.note: The page's Grand Dukes table also lists John I Albert as a disputed Grand Duke 1492-1501.

rulers.name: Alexander Jagiellon
rulers.title: King of Poland from 1501, Grand Duke of Lithuania since 1492

rulers.name: Sigismund I the Old
rulers.note: Grand Duke from 1506; the Kings table gives 1507-1548.

rulers.name: Sigismund II Augustus
rulers.note: Co-ruler from 1529, sole ruler from 1548; reigns to his death in 1572 (the dynasty page tables give 1572), but this dossier ends with the Union of Lublin in 1569.

correction.text: unchanged shape; status only: the Masovian duchies (149 of the shape's cells) are fiefs of the Polish crown until 1526 and are drawn in the vassal tint; the vassal_start and vassal_end events carry it

keyframe_review.note: 1,030,905 km2 for 1450-1452. The shape is Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland of 1449 plus its Grand Duchy of Lithuania of 1449 (4,454 cells in common; the shape has 4,456, the two 1449 shapes together 4,462), so it stands for the two states in personal union under Casimir IV. Area check: the Union of Lublin page puts the Commonwealth at 'some 400,000 square miles (1,000,000 km2)' at its apogee, and Cliopatria's shape peaks at 1,054,018 km2 (within a few percent); the Muscovite-Lithuanian Wars page says the 1503 loss of 210,000 km2 was roughly a third of Lithuania (about 630,000 km2 before), against 815,401 km2 for Cliopatria's 1449 Grand Duchy (ratio 1.3). The Masovia page: a fiefdom of Poland 1385-1569 (infobox) and incorporated in 1526; the same status note applies to every shape to 1525.

1,030,949 km2: the 1450 outline with 44 km2 of difference (no change). The page has Casimir IV as King of Poland from 1447 and Grand Duke from 1440, so both halves are ruled together throughout. Masovia fief status as for _1450.
1,030,883 km2: the same outline again (no cell changes). Masovia fief status as for _1450.

correction.text: the 1459 outline for 1463-1465: the Teutonic lands the shape adds in 1463 (Pomerelia and western Prussia, 89 cells) are the zone of the Thirteen Years' War, contested until the Second Peace of Thorn of October 1466; the shape with Royal Prussia holds from 1466 (see _1466)

keyframe_review.note: 1,050,669 km2: the 1463 shape takes 89 cells (22,517 km2; 84 of them in the gazetteer's West Prussia, 67 in Pomerelia) from the Teutonic Order, which falls from 273 to 185 cells. The page dates the allegiance of the Prussian Confederation to 6 March 1454 and the peace to October 1466 ('an autonomous Polish province, later known as Royal Prussia'), and dates no 1463 event: Mewe fell on 1 January 1464 and Konitz on 28 September 1466.

union.text: the Prince-Bishopric of Warmia, which came under the Polish crown after the Peace of Thorn

correction.text: the 1463 shape with Royal Prussia plus the Prince-Bishopric of Warmia, which the page puts under the Polish crown after the Second Peace of Thorn (October 1466)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria adds Warmia (22 cells taken from the Teutonic Order, 18 of them in the gazetteer's Warmia) only in 1468; the page has 'the Bishopric of Warmia came under the Polish crown' with the 1466 peace. The Kingdom of Poland page calls Warmia 'a protectorate of Kingdom of Poland' from 1466 to 1772; it is drawn direct as Cliopatria draws it.

1,053,746 km2: Royal Prussia and Warmia (22 more Teutonic cells, 18 of them in Warmia) held. Also changed in 1468 and unexplained by any page opened: +10 cells on the Black Sea coast (29.4-34.7 E, 47.4-49.3 N, the Crimean Khanate's in 1463) and -14 cells scattered over the west and south. Masovia fief status as for _1450.
1,053,791 km2: the 1468 outline (+44 km2, no cell change). Masovia fief status as for _1450.
1,054,018 km2, 1482-1491, the largest shape: +2 cells (31.4-31.6 E, 57.1 N) from the Novgorod Republic, which no page opened explains (unverified: page budget). Masovia fief status as for _1450.

correction.text: unchanged shape, right for 1492-1493 only: the Muscovite war of 1492-1494 ends with the 'eternal' peace of 5 February 1494, which takes Vyazma and the upper Oka (keyframe _1494)

keyframe_review.note: 1,053,974 km2 (-44 km2, no cell change). The page puts the loss in 1494 while Cliopatria draws it in 1497; the shape is therefore right for 1492-1493 and the 1494-1496 years take _1494.

correction.text: the 1497 outline carried back to 1494: Lithuania without the Principality of Vyazma and the upper Oka region lost to Moscow by the peace of 5 February 1494

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page: 'An "eternal" peace treaty was concluded on February 5, 1494' and the lost area is estimated at about 87,000 km2. Cliopatria's loss is 143 cells (36,179 km2), 139 of them in Moscow's 1497 shape (32.9-36.0 E, 53.9-56.8 N): ratio 2.4 to the page, outside a factor of two. The shape is kept; the page's figure may take in claims the shape does not.
1,021,300 km2 for 1497-1501: the post-1494 outline, 3 cells gained in Podolia (30.9-31.9 E, 48.0-48.5 N) unexplained. John I Albert's Moldavian campaign of 1497 (Cosmin Forest) moved no border.

correction.text: unchanged shape, right for 1502 only: the six-year truce of 25 March 1503 takes Chernigov, Novgorod-Seversk, Starodub and the upper Oka (keyframe _1503)

keyframe_review.note: 1,022,105 km2; +7/-6 cells (30.3-38.1 E) unexplained. The page puts the loss in March 1503, Cliopatria in 1507.

correction.text: the 1507 outline carried back to 1503, without Gomel's district: Lithuania without Chernigov, Novgorod-Seversk, Starodub and the lands around the upper Oka, lost to Moscow by the truce of 25 March 1503, and without Gomel, which was Muscovite after the war of 1500-1503 until 1535

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page: Lithuania lost about 210,000 km2, roughly a third of its territory (70 volosts, 22 towns, 13 villages by Liubavskii). Cliopatria's loss is 1,049 cells (265,397 km2, ratio 1.26): 677 cells in Moscow's 1507 shape and 372 in the steppe east of the Dnieper (33.6-38.0 E, 48.6-52.4 N) that no neighbour holds, which the loss event files under nobody. Gomel (a 60 km disc, 51 cells, 41 of them in this Cliopatria outline, which draws Gomel as Lithuanian throughout) is cut from 1503 to 1534: the Gomel page has Semyon, who held it 'from 1483 to 1505', 'transferred it to the Grand Principality of Moscow', says Lithuania 'tried to regain Gomel' in the war of 1500-1503 and failed, and has Lithuanian and Polish forces retake it in 1535; the Muscovite-Lithuanian Wars page does not name Gomel in the 1503 truce.

780,062 km2 for 1507-1511. The 8 October 1508 peace 'maintained the territorial accords of the 1503 truce', so the outline stands through 1511. Gomel (a 60 km disc, 51 cells, 41 of them in this Cliopatria outline, which draws Gomel as Lithuanian throughout) is cut from 1503 to 1534: the Gomel page has Semyon, who held it 'from 1483 to 1505', 'transferred it to the Grand Principality of Moscow', says Lithuania 'tried to regain Gomel' in the war of 1500-1503 and failed, and has Lithuanian and Polish forces retake it in 1535; the Muscovite-Lithuanian Wars page does not name Gomel in the 1503 truce.

correction.text: the Cliopatria outline of 1507 without Gomel's district, right for 1507-1511 (Gomel Muscovite until 1535)
the Cliopatria outline of 1512 without Gomel's district, right for 1512-1513 only: Smolensk falls in July 1514 (keyframe _1514)

keyframe_review.note: 780,207 km2. Moscow invaded in December 1512 and its sieges of Smolensk in 1513 failed (page). Gomel (a 60 km disc, 51 cells, 41 of them in this Cliopatria outline, which draws Gomel as Lithuanian throughout) is cut from 1503 to 1534: the Gomel page has Semyon, who held it 'from 1483 to 1505', 'transferred it to the Grand Principality of Moscow', says Lithuania 'tried to regain Gomel' in the war of 1500-1503 and failed, and has Lithuanian and Polish forces retake it in 1535; the Muscovite-Lithuanian Wars page does not name Gomel in the 1503 truce.

correction.text: the 1519 outline carried back to 1514, without Gomel's district: Lithuania without Smolensk, which fell to Moscow in July 1514 and stayed Muscovite under the 1522 truce

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Cliopatria takes Smolensk's land from Lithuania in two steps, 101 cells in 1516 and 94 cells in 1519 (195 cells, 49,335 km2), against the page's about 56,000 km2 lost in the war (ratio 0.88); the page dates the fall to July 1514 and Orsha (8 September 1514) did not bring it back. The same two steps add 42 cells (29.3-31.7 E, 55.7-56.9 N) in 1516 and 22 cells (30.6-31.5 E, 52.5-56.0 N) in 1519 from Moscow, which no page opened explains; the 1519 outline keeps them (unverified: page budget). Gomel (a 60 km disc, 51 cells, 41 of them in this Cliopatria outline, which draws Gomel as Lithuanian throughout) is cut from 1503 to 1534: the Gomel page has Semyon, who held it 'from 1483 to 1505', 'transferred it to the Grand Principality of Moscow', says Lithuania 'tried to regain Gomel' in the war of 1500-1503 and failed, and has Lithuanian and Polish forces retake it in 1535; the Muscovite-Lithuanian Wars page does not name Gomel in the 1503 truce.

correction.text: use the 1514-1518 keyframe, which is the 1519 outline without Gomel's district: Smolensk is lost in full from 1514, not in two steps

keyframe_review.note: 766,120 km2 for 1516-1518: only about half of the Smolensk land is cut here; the page has Smolensk lost as a whole in July 1514.

correction.text: the Cliopatria outline of 1519 without Gomel's district, right for 1519-1534; Gomel is back from 1535 (keyframe _1535)

keyframe_review.note: 751,125 km2 for 1519-1539: the post-Smolensk outline. It draws Gomel's district as Lithuanian (41 of the 51 cells of a 60 km disc); the Gomel page has Gomel Muscovite from the war of 1500-1503 until the Lithuanian recapture of 1535, so the disc is cut for 1519-1534 and returns in keyframe _1535. Starodub is not added: the Muscovite-Lithuanian Wars page says the forces 'took Gomel and Starodub' in 1534-1537 but names only Homel as left to the king by the truce, and Cliopatria's Moscow shape of 1540 holds all of Starodub's disc.

correction.text: the Cliopatria outline of 1519 with Gomel's district back from Moscow, retaken by Lithuanian and Polish forces in 1535 and left to the king by the five-year truce of 1537

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (replaces the Starodub keyframe _1537 of the first pass). The Gomel page: Radvila's, Tarnowski's and Niemirowicz's forces retook the city in 1535 'after the surrender of Moscow's deputy', and by the peace of 1537 'Gomel together with its volost remained a Lithuanian possession'; the Muscovite-Lithuanian Wars page: 'Homel stayed under the king's control, while Moscow kept Sebezh and Zavoloche'. The 1519 outline holds 41 of the 51 cells of the Gomel disc. Starodub: the Wars page says it was taken in the war but does not say it stayed Lithuanian (its truce passage names Homel only), the first-pass 60 km disc was wholly inside Moscow's 1540 shape, and it is dropped. The table's 'Gained 20,000 km2' for 1537 is not explained by Gomel's 12,900 km2 disc and stays unexplained.
751,417 km2, 1540-1546 (+1 cell at 22.3 E 49.2 N, the Polish south-east): the 1519 outline unchanged, as for _1535; Starodub is not added (see _1535).
751,260 km2, 1547-1555 (-2 cells at 22.9-23.9 E, 48.6-49.0 N, both in the Eastern Hungarian Kingdom's 1547 shape; the pages opened date no frontier change there). Starodub is not added (see _1535).

751,282 km2 for 1556-1563, right for 1556-1560; the 1561-1563 years take _1561. In June 1559 the estates of Livonia come under Polish-Lithuanian protection (first Treaty of Vilnius) but stay a separate state until 1561. Starodub is not added (see _1535).

union.text: Vidzeme and Latgale with south-western Estonia, the Order's land ceded to the Grand Duchy at Vilnius, less the east Muscovy held (Cliopatria's Tsardom of Russia 1564 shape) and the Danish coast (its Denmark-Norway 1564 shape)

correction.text: the 1556 outline with the Livonian land that the Treaty of Vilnius (28 November 1561) gave the Grand Duchy: Vidzeme, Latgale and south-western Estonia, without the Muscovite-held east, the Danish coast and Courland and Semigallia (a vassal duchy from 1562)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Cliopatria adds 109 cells (27,577 km2; 21.1-26.0 E, 55.9-57.5 N) only in 1564 from its Livonian Conference, and 86 of them lie in the gazetteer's Courland, the vassal duchy of ledger 28 (a Courland drawn direct would be drawn twice); only 22 are in Vidzeme or Latgale. The Duchy of Livonia page: by the Treaty of Vilnius of 28 November 1561 'the south-western part of today's Estonia and the north-eastern part of today's Latvia, covering what are now Vidzeme and Latgale' went to the Grand Duchy; the Muscovite-Lithuanian Wars table has 'Gained 85,000 km2' for 1561. The correction takes the 1556 outline and adds the gazetteer regions Livonia and Latgale, less the east Muscovy held (Dorpat, Narva, Fellin and 'many lesser fortresses', Livonian War page) as Cliopatria's Tsardom of Russia 1564 shape draws it and the Danish coast (Ösel-Wiek); Estonia north of that went to Sweden. The added land is 225 cells (about 57,000 km2 on the gazetteer's cell area) and the Courland vassal duchy (about 29,000 km2) is the rest of the page's 85,000 km2, so the factor of 3.1 of the first pass falls to about 1.0. Courland and Semigallia is not in this direct shape: it is the vassal duchy of ledger 28 from 1562.

union.text: Vidzeme and Latgale with south-western Estonia, the Order's land ceded to the Grand Duchy at Vilnius, less the east Muscovy held (Cliopatria's Tsardom of Russia 1564 shape) and the Danish coast (its Denmark-Norway 1564 shape)

correction.text: the same outline as _1561, right for 1564-1569 only: Cliopatria's 1564 shape holds Courland (86 of its 109 added cells) and little of Livonia; the state ends with the Union of Lublin of 1 July 1569 and the 1570-1571 years belong to the Commonwealth; Courland and Semigallia is a vassal duchy of the Grand Duchy from 1562 and is not in the direct shape

keyframe_review.note: 776,290 km2 for 1564-1571 as Cliopatria draws it. The corrected outline is the 1556 outline plus 225 cells of Livonia (about 803,000 km2 on Cliopatria's area basis, about 877,000 on the gazetteer's cell area, which runs 9% above the Area column), ratio to the 1,000,000 km2 of the Union of Lublin page's footnote about 0.8 to 0.9. The page makes the Commonwealth one state from 1569 and the Duchy of Livonia a joint domain of the Crown and the Grand Duchy; Cliopatria draws the Commonwealth only from 1572, so 1570-1571 is a handover for the Commonwealth dossier. The Kingdom of Poland page has Courland and Semigallia as 'a vassal state of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania' from 1562, which Cliopatria draws direct.

region.text: the Crown of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania under one ruler

ledger.note: 1450: Poland and Lithuania are drawn as one Jagiellonian realm. Casimir IV was Grand Duke of Lithuania from 1440 and King of Poland from 1447 ('Grand Dukes of Lithuania (1377-1392 and 1440-1572)'); the dynasty's founding year on the page is 1386. Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland and Grand Duchy of Lithuania rows both end in 1449.

region.text: the Crown of Poland

ledger.note: 1450: the Crown of Poland (Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland of 1449) is drawn inside the Jagiellonian realm.

region.text: the Grand Duchy of Lithuania

ledger.note: 1450: the Grand Duchy of Lithuania (Cliopatria's shape of 1449) is drawn inside the Jagiellonian realm; the two states stay distinct until the Union of Lublin of 1569.

region.text: the Duchy of Masovia, a fief of the Polish crown

ledger.note: 1450: the Masovian duchies are Polish fiefs. The page: 'in 1351 he and his brother Casimir became vassals of the Polish kings'; its infobox gives a fiefdom of Poland for 1385-1569. Status already in force when the Jagiellon realm begins; the Masovian voivodeship holds 149 of the realm's cells.

region.text: the Principality of Moldavia, whose ruler had become a vassal of Władysław II

ledger.note: 1450: Moldavia is a vassal of the Polish crown, a status already in force when the realm begins. The Kingdom of Poland page, under the heading 'Principality of Moldavia (1387–1497)': Petru I, 'becoming a vassal of Władysław II on September 26, 1387'. The section describes no later homage, and says that Petru Aron's rule 'also signified the beginning of Moldavia's Ottoman Empire allegiance', so the allegiance was divided from the 1450s. Confidence 2: the page gives the start and the heading's end year, not the state of the relation in 1450.

region.text: the Teutonic lands that became Royal Prussia: Pomerelia and the western part of Prussia (Cliopatria's 1463 shape less its 1459 shape)

ledger.note: March 1454: the Thirteen Years' War begins over Prussia. The Prussian Confederation rebelled against the Teutonic Grand Master in February and 'delegates of the Prussian Confederation pledged allegiance to Casimir on 6 March 1454'; Poland's declaration of war was predated to 22 February. Land held by the Confederation and Poland is contested until 1466.

region.text: the Duchy of Oświęcim: Oświęcim and Kęty, two ducal castles and 45 villages

ledger.note: 1457: Casimir IV buys the Duchy of Oświęcim. The page: the duchy 'had fallen under the Bohemian vassalage' (Jan I's homage to John of Bohemia in 1327), Jan IV, the last duke, 'declared himself a vassal' of King Casimir in 1454, had no male heir and sold the duchy 'three years later' for 3,000,000 Prague groschen; the introduction says it was 'sold to the Kingdom of Poland in 1457'. Cliopatria already draws the land inside the realm from 1450 (1 of the 3 cells of a 15 km disc, Bohemia holds 2), so this event records the acquisition and no keyframe is cut. The duchy needs a dossier (duchy-of-oswiecim).

region.text: the Teutonic lands that became Royal Prussia: Pomerelia and the western part of Prussia (Cliopatria's 1463 shape less its 1459 shape)

ledger.note: October 1466: the Second Peace of Thorn ends the war (the article says 10 October, its infobox 19 October 1466).

region.text: the Teutonic lands that became Royal Prussia: Pomerelia and the western part of Prussia (Cliopatria's 1463 shape less its 1459 shape)

ledger.note: October 1466: Pomerelia and western Prussia become Polish. The page: western Prussia became 'an autonomous Polish province, later known as Royal Prussia', and Pomerelia was returned. Cliopatria draws the gain in 1463.

region.text: the Prince-Bishopric of Warmia, which came under the Polish crown after the Peace of Thorn

ledger.note: October 1466: the Prince-Bishopric of Warmia comes under the Polish crown (Thorn page); the Kingdom of Poland page calls it 'a protectorate of Kingdom of Poland' to 1772. Cliopatria draws it in 1468.

region.text: Eastern Prussia, which remained under the Teutonic Knights

ledger.note: October 1466: the Order becomes the Polish king's vassal. 'Eastern Prussia remained under the control of the Teutonic Knights, although it became a vassal of the Polish king'; the Grand Master became a senator of the Polish kingdom.

region.text: the Principality of Vyazma and a sizable region in the upper reaches of the Oka River (Cliopatria's 1492 shape less its 1497 shape, where Moscow holds it)

ledger.note: August 1492: Ivan III invades Lithuania. 'In August 1492, without declaring war, Ivan III began large military actions'; border attacks on the upper Oka princedoms had begun around 1486-1487.

region.text: the Duchy of Zator

ledger.note: 1494: Jan V, the last of the Zator brothers and its sole ruler in 1494, decides 'in the same year to sell the duchy to King John I Albert of Poland', with a guarantee (as the page's text goes) that he remain duke until his death; 'Jan was killed in 1513 and Zator was united with Poland', and the Sejm of 1564 incorporated both duchies. The sale is dated 1494 and the union with the Crown 1513. Cliopatria draws the land inside the realm from 1450 (3 of 3 cells of a 15 km disc), so this event records the acquisition and no keyframe is cut. The duchy (split from Oświęcim in 1445) needs a dossier (duchy-of-zator).

region.text: the Principality of Vyazma and a sizable region in the upper reaches of the Oka River (Cliopatria's 1492 shape less its 1497 shape, where Moscow holds it)

ledger.note: 5 February 1494: the 'eternal' peace ends the first Muscovite-Lithuanian war.

region.text: the Principality of Vyazma and a sizable region in the upper reaches of the Oka River (Cliopatria's 1492 shape less its 1497 shape, where Moscow holds it)

ledger.note: 5 February 1494: Lithuania gives up Vyazma and the upper Oka to Moscow. 'An "eternal" peace treaty was concluded on February 5, 1494', the first Lithuanian territorial losses to Moscow; the page estimates the lost area at about 87,000 km2 (Cliopatria 1497: 35,000 km2 held by Moscow).

region.text: the Principality of Moldavia

ledger.note: 1497: the end year of the page's heading 'Principality of Moldavia (1387–1497)'; the section does not say how the vassalage ended. In 1497 John I Albert's campaign to put his brother Sigismund on the Moldavian throne failed (siege of Suceava, defeat in the Cosmin Forest, 26 October 1497; Cosmin Forest page), and the page there says nothing of suzerainty. Confidence 2: the year is the heading's, the manner is not on the page.

region.text: Chernigov, Novgorod-Seversk, Starodub and the lands around the upper Oka (Cliopatria's 1502 shape less its 1507 shape, where Moscow holds it)

ledger.note: 1500: the second war with Moscow. 'On July 14, 1500, the Lithuanians suffered a great defeat in the Battle of Vedrosha' and Grand Hetman Ostrogski was captured; Bryansk, Dorogobuzh, Toropets and Putivl were overrun in 1500 (page).

region.text: Chernigov, Novgorod-Seversk, Starodub and the lands around the upper Oka (Cliopatria's 1502 shape less its 1507 shape, where Moscow holds it)

ledger.note: 25 March 1503: a six-year truce ends the war.

region.text: Chernigov, Novgorod-Seversk, Starodub and the lands around the upper Oka (Cliopatria's 1502 shape less its 1507 shape, where Moscow holds it)

ledger.note: 25 March 1503: Lithuania loses about a third of its land to Moscow. The truce gave Moscow 'Chernigov, Novgorod-Seversk, Starodub, and lands around the upper Oka River', about 210,000 km2; Lithuania also acknowledged Ivan III as sovereign of all Russia. The 8 October 1508 peace kept the accords.

region.text: Gomel and its district

ledger.note: 1503: Gomel is Muscovite when the war of 1500-1503 ends. The Gomel page has Semyon, who held it 'from 1483 to 1505', transfer it to the Grand Principality of Moscow, and says Lithuania 'tried to regain Gomel and other lands transferred to Moscow' in the war and 'had suffered defeat'; the Muscovite-Lithuanian Wars page does not name Gomel in the 1503 truce. The transfer is undated on the page, so the year is the truce's and the region is the 60 km disc of the dossier; Cliopatria draws Gomel's district as Lithuanian in every shape from 1502 to 1540 (51 of 51 cells to 1506, 41 from 1507, 32 in the 1516 shape). Retaken in 1535.

region.text: the left-bank steppe east of the Dnieper that Cliopatria's 1507 shape also drops and that Moscow's shape does not hold

ledger.note: 1503: the part of Cliopatria's 1507 loss that Moscow does not hold, the steppe east of the Dnieper (372 cells, 94,000 km2). The page lists towns and the upper Oka, not these lands: bridging from the shape. The Wild Fields page (opened in the repair pass) does not date or assign these lands: it describes the steppe of the 15th-16th centuries as a borderland of 'Crimean-Nogai Raids' that caused 'considerable devastation and depopulation', not as one state's land, which supports a stateless reading but not the loss itself; confidence stays 1.

region.text: Smolensk and its land: the cells Cliopatria takes from Lithuania in 1516 and 1519 and gives to Moscow

ledger.note: December 1512: Moscow invades again. Its sieges of Smolensk in 1513 failed (page); the zone is the land Cliopatria takes in 1516 and 1519.

region.text: Smolensk and its land: the cells Cliopatria takes from Lithuania in 1516 and 1519 and gives to Moscow

ledger.note: July 1514: Smolensk falls to Moscow and is never returned. The city 'fell in July 1514'; 'On 8 September 1514, the Russians suffered a major defeat at the Battle of Orsha' but Smolensk stayed lost; Lithuania lost about 56,000 km2 in the war. Cliopatria draws the loss in 1516 and 1519.

region.text: Smolensk and its land: the cells Cliopatria takes from Lithuania in 1516 and 1519 and gives to Moscow

ledger.note: 1522: a five-year truce 'for Russia to retain control of Smolensk' ends the war; it was later extended to 1534.

region.text: the Teutonic Order's Prussian state

ledger.note: April 1525: the Order's rule in Prussia ends. The Treaty of Kraków of 8 April 1525 ended the Polish-Teutonic War and, two days later, Albert resigned as Grand Master (the Kingdom of Poland page: he 'secularized the Prussian State of the Teutonic Order').

region.text: the Duchy of Prussia, held 'as a fief of the Kingdom of Poland'

ledger.note: 10 April 1525: Albert pays the Prussian Homage at Kraków. 'Albert resigned as Grand Master and received the title Duke of Prussia from Polish King Sigismund'; the duchy is a Polish fief. Cliopatria's Duchy of Prussia row starts in 1526.

region.text: the Duchy of Masovia, a fief of the Polish crown

ledger.note: 1526: the Duchy of Masovia ends. 'In 1526, the country was incorporated into the Kingdom of Poland' and became the Masovian Voivodeship of the Polish Crown after Janusz III's death.

region.text: Gomel and its district

ledger.note: 1534: war over the Chernigov-Starodub border. In the summer of 1534 Jerzy Radziwiłł and the Tatars raided Chernigov, Starodub and Briansk, and Lithuanian and Polish forces then 'took Gomel and Starodub' in response (no date on the Wars page; the Gomel page has Gomel retaken in 1535). The zone is Gomel, the one place the truce text assigns; Starodub, taken in the war, is left out because the page does not give its later status.

region.text: Gomel and its district

ledger.note: 1535: Lithuanian and Polish forces retake Gomel. The Gomel page: Radvila, Tarnowski and Niemirowicz retook the city in 1535 'after the surrender of Moscow's deputy', and by the peace of 1537 'Gomel together with its volost remained a Lithuanian possession' (the Muscovite-Lithuanian Wars page agrees: 'Homel stayed under the king's control'). The Wars page says the forces 'took Gomel and Starodub' but not that Starodub stayed Lithuanian, so no Starodub gain is recorded; its table's 'Gained 20,000 km2' for 1537 is more than the 12,900 km2 disc and stays unexplained. Moscow's side: a loss of Gomel in 1535.

region.text: Gomel and its district

ledger.note: 1537: a five-year truce without prisoner exchange ends the war (the page gives no date). The truce is one 'in which Homel stayed under the king's control, while Moscow kept Sebezh and Zavoloche'; Starodub is not named in it.

region.text: the estates of Livonia

ledger.note: June 1559: Livonia comes under Polish-Lithuanian protection. 'In June 1559, the estates of Livonia came under Polish-Lithuanian protection through the first Treaty of Vilnius.' The Livonian War had begun on 22 January 1558 with Ivan IV's invasion.

region.text: the lands of the Livonian Order

ledger.note: 28 November 1561: the protectorate over Livonia ends with annexation. The Duchy of Livonia page: by the Treaty of Vilnius 'the Livonian nobility accepted the suzerainty of the Grand Duke of Lithuania' and kept their privileges; the Livonian War page: 'The weakened Livonian Order was dissolved by the second Treaty of Vilnius in 1561'.

minus.text: Vidzeme and Latgale with south-western Estonia, the Order's land ceded to the Grand Duchy at Vilnius, less the east Muscovy held (Cliopatria's Tsardom of Russia 1564 shape) and the Danish coast (its Denmark-Norway 1564 shape)

region.text: Livonia: Vidzeme, Latgale and south-western Estonia, the Order's land that the Treaty of Vilnius gave the Grand Duchy, less the Muscovite-held east, the Danish coast and the land already held in 1556

ledger.note: 28 November 1561: Lithuania takes the Order's land in Livonia. The Duchy of Livonia page: 'the south-western part of today's Estonia and the north-eastern part of today's Latvia, covering what are now Vidzeme and Latgale' were ceded to the Grand Duchy; the Muscovite-Lithuanian Wars table has 'Gained 85,000 km2 ... Gained Duchy of Livonia by the Treaty of Vilnius (1561)'. The first pass drew Cliopatria's 1564 addition, which is mostly Courland (86 of 109 cells, the vassal duchy of ledger 28) and so about 27,600 km2. The region is now the Livonian land proper, 225 cells (about 57,000 km2); with the Courland duchy (about 29,000 km2) it comes to the page's 85,000 km2. Estonia north of it went to Sweden, Ösel-Wiek to Denmark, and Muscovy kept Dorpat, Narva and Fellin (Livonian War page); confidence 2 because the Muscovite-held east is drawn from Cliopatria's Tsardom of Russia shape of 1564.

region.text: Courland and Semigallia, the duchy of Gotthard Kettler: the region less the land the Grand Duchy already held in 1556

ledger.note: 1562: the Duchy of Courland and Semigallia begins 'as a vassal state of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania' (Kingdom of Poland page), under Gotthard Kettler, the Order's last master and first Duke of Courland (Livonian War page). Cliopatria draws it as direct Lithuanian land (86 of its 1564 additions are in Courland); here it is the vassal tint and is not in the direct keyframes from 1561.

region.text: Courland and Semigallia, the duchy of Gotthard Kettler: the region less the land the Grand Duchy already held in 1556

ledger.note: 1 July 1569: the Grand Duchy becomes part of the Commonwealth, whose joint sovereignty takes over the Livonian lands; Courland and Semigallia stays a vassal duchy of the Commonwealth (relation carried by the Commonwealth dossier).

region.text: the Duchy of Prussia

ledger.note: 1569: the suzerainty over the Duchy of Prussia passes to the Commonwealth; on 19 July 1569 at Lublin Albert Frederick paid homage to Sigismund II Augustus (Prussian Homage page), and the Polish fief lasted to the Treaty of Bromberg (1657).

region.text: the Crown of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania

ledger.note: 1 July 1569: the Union of Lublin merges Poland and Lithuania. The union was signed 'on 1 July 1569 in Lublin, Poland' (the page also has the final act signed on 4 July); before it the king annexed Podlachia, Volhynia, Bracław and Kyiv from the Grand Duchy to the Crown ('on 6 June'). The Duchy of Livonia becomes a Polish-Lithuanian condominium, and Royal Prussia's autonomy is largely abandoned.

region.text: the Crown of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania

ledger.note: 1 July 1569: the Jagiellonian union ends in the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. The Kingdom of Poland page: 'The Union of Lublin created the single state of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth on July 1, 1569'; Sigismund II Augustus, the last Jagiellon king, reigned to 1572.

wars.name: Thirteen Years' War

zones.text: the Teutonic lands that became Royal Prussia: Pomerelia and the western part of Prussia (Cliopatria's 1463 shape less its 1459 shape)
the Prince-Bishopric of Warmia, which came under the Polish crown after the Peace of Thorn

wars.outcome: The Second Peace of Thorn (October 1466) gave Poland western Prussia as Royal Prussia, Pomerelia and the Bishopric of Warmia; eastern Prussia stayed with the Order as a vassal of the Polish king.
wars.note: Timeline of the page: the Confederation's act of disobedience 4 February 1454, Casimir's acceptance 6 March 1454, Marienburg's castles transferred to the Polish army 6 June 1457 and the town on 5 July 1460, Schwetz 1461, Mewe 1 January 1464, Konitz 28 September 1466.

wars.name: Muscovite-Lithuanian War (1487-1494)

zones.text: the Principality of Vyazma and a sizable region in the upper reaches of the Oka River (Cliopatria's 1492 shape less its 1497 shape, where Moscow holds it)

wars.outcome: Moscow took the Principality of Vyazma and a region on the upper Oka; 'eternal' peace of 5 February 1494.
wars.note: Border attacks from about 1486-1487 with Moscow's Crimean ally Meñli I Giray; large operations from August 1492; war formally declared 1493.

wars.name: Muscovite-Lithuanian War (1500-1503)

zones.text: Chernigov, Novgorod-Seversk, Starodub and the lands around the upper Oka (Cliopatria's 1502 shape less its 1507 shape, where Moscow holds it)
Gomel and its district: transferred to Moscow by Semyon and not regained in the war

wars.outcome: Lithuanian defeats at Vedrosha (14 July 1500) and Mstislavl (November 1501); the truce of 25 March 1503 gave Moscow about 210,000 km2 including Chernigov, Novgorod-Seversk and Starodub.

wars.name: Muscovite-Lithuanian War (1507-1508)
wars.outcome: Sigismund I asked for the return of the 1503 gains; Glinski's rebellion ran alongside; the 'eternal peace' of 8 October 1508 kept the accords of the 1503 truce. No border moved.

wars.name: Muscovite-Lithuanian War (1512-1522)

zones.text: Smolensk and its land: the cells Cliopatria takes from Lithuania in 1516 and 1519 and gives to Moscow

wars.outcome: Smolensk fell in July 1514 and was kept by Moscow under the five-year truce of 1522; Lithuania won at Orsha on 8 September 1514 but lost about 56,000 km2.

wars.name: Polish-Teutonic War (1519-1521)
wars.outcome: The Polish General Sejm declared war in December 1519 and fighting began in January 1520; the armistice of Thorn of 5 April 1521 ended it; the Treaty of Kraków of 1525 secularised the Order's state as the Duchy of Prussia, a Polish fief.
wars.note: The page gives no frontier change for 1519-1521 (no zone drawn, no ledger event); the 1525 settlement is ledger 'vassal_end teutonic-order' and 'vassal_start duchy-of-prussia'. The page's infobox lists a Polish victory.

wars.name: Muscovite-Lithuanian War (1534-1537)
wars.outcome: Lithuanian and Polish forces took Gomel and Starodub; the five-year truce left Homel to the king while Moscow kept Sebezh and Zavoloche; Starodub is not named in the truce.
wars.note: Starodub (taken in the war per the page, status after the truce not given) is not in the zone; the first pass drew it as a Lithuanian gain of 1537 and the reviewer found that the page does not say so. The Gomel page dates the recapture of Gomel to 1535.

wars.name: Polish-Moldavian campaign of John I Albert (1497)
wars.outcome: The siege of Suceava (24 September to 19 October 1497) failed and the Poles were defeated in the Cosmin Forest (26 October 1497, the text says the battle began on the night of 25 October); Poland sued for peace in 1499. No border moved.
wars.note: 'John's primary goal was to place his brother, Sigismund, on the Moldavian throne' (page); the defeat 'dissuaded the Polish king from challenging Ottoman supremacy on the Black Sea'. The Cosmin Forest page says nothing of Polish suzerainty over Moldavia; the Kingdom of Poland page dates the vassalage 1387-1497 (ledger: vassal_start 1450, vassal_end 1497).

wars.name: Livonian War

minus.text: Vidzeme and Latgale with south-western Estonia, the Order's land ceded to the Grand Duchy at Vilnius, less the east Muscovy held (Cliopatria's Tsardom of Russia 1564 shape) and the Danish coast (its Denmark-Norway 1564 shape)

zones.text: Livonia: Vidzeme, Latgale and south-western Estonia, the Order's land that passed to Lithuania in 1561 (less the Muscovite-held east and the Danish coast)

wars.outcome: Livonia came under Polish-Lithuanian protection in June 1559 and was annexed in 1561 when the Order was dissolved; Estonia went to Sweden; the war ran to 1583 (Truce of Jam Zapolski 1582: Russia surrendered its Livonian holdings, Polotsk stayed with the Commonwealth).
wars.note: The page gives 22 January 1558 to 10 August 1583; only the years to 1569 concern this dossier. A three-year truce with Russia was signed in June 1570.

certainty.note: The level is the realm-wide minimum: the Muscovite, Tatar and steppe frontiers are approximate, and the Teutonic frontier in Prussia is drawn from Cliopatria's outline, not from a treaty line, until the Second Peace of Thorn.

The level is the realm-wide minimum: the steppe, forest and Tatar frontiers stay soft throughout. Exceptions: the Prussian frontier is sharp from the Second Peace of Thorn (October 1466), and the Muscovite frontier follows named towns after the treaties of 1494, 1503, 1508, 1522 and 1537.

notes: House of Jagiellon, eu-15-i, 9 pages (budget up to 9). (1) What the row is: Cliopatria's House of Jagiellon (1450-1571) is the union of its Kingdom of Poland and Grand Duchy of Lithuania rows of 1449 (4,456 cells against 4,462), both of which end in 1449, and is replaced by its Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth row in 1572. The dossier therefore stands for the Jagiellonian Poland-Lithuania of 1450-1569 (type dynasty, drawn as one state), with the two merge events at 1450 naming the two predecessors; the kingdom-of-poland and grand-duchy-of-lithuania dossiers of the other parts should end in 1449 or declare that the Jagiellon dossier carries 1450-1569, and the Commonwealth dossier should start in 1569. Cliopatria's 1570-1571 shapes are therefore handed to the Commonwealth. The orchestrator must reconcile the three. (2) Life: the dynasty page founds the dynasty in 1386 and has Casimir IV in both thrones from 1447; start 1450 follows Cliopatria. The end follows the Union of Lublin ('on 1 July 1569', the page also has the act signed on 4 July) rather than Sigismund II Augustus's death (1572, tables) or the infobox's 'Dissolution: 1596'. (3) Vassals: Masovia 1450-1526 (page: fiefdom of Poland 1385-1569 in the infobox, incorporated in 1526; the incorporation of Płock and Rawa in 1495 is unclear on the page), the Teutonic Order in eastern Prussia 1466-1525, the Duchy of Prussia 1525-1569 (continued by the Commonwealth to 1657), Livonia 1559-1561, Courland and Semigallia 1562-1569. The kingdom-of-poland ledger and the Masovia dossier of the other parts, and the Prussia, Livonia and Courland dossiers, should carry the matching vassal-side entries. Moldavia: the Kingdom of Poland page says Petru I became a vassal of Władysław II on 26 September 1387 under the heading 'Principality of Moldavia (1387–1497)'; the repair pass records vassal_start 1450 and vassal_end 1497 at confidence 2 (the page gives no homage after 1387 and no manner of ending, and says Petru Aron's rule began Moldavia's Ottoman allegiance). (4) Cliopatria quirks: loss dates are 2-4 years late (Thorn 1463 vs 1466; Vyazma 1497 vs 1494; Chernigov 1507 vs 1503; Smolensk 1516 and 1519 vs 1514) and Gomel (Muscovite from the war of 1500-1503, retaken 1535) is drawn Lithuanian throughout; new keyframes carry the corrected years. The first pass added a Starodub gain of 1537 that the Muscovite-Lithuanian Wars page does not support (the truce passage names only Homel), and it was removed in the repair pass. The small unexplained changes (1468 Black Sea +10 and -14 cells, 1482 +2 cells, 1497 +3 cells, 1502 +7/-6 cells, 1516 +42 cells, 1519 +22 cells, 1540 +1, 1547 -2 cells to the Eastern Hungarian Kingdom) are kept as Cliopatria draws them (unverified: page budget). The 1,049-cell loss of 1503 includes 372 cells of steppe that no neighbour holds; they are filed as a confidence-1 loss to nobody. (5) Not done: Siewierz (1443 sold to the Archbishop of Kraków per the Kingdom of Poland page) and Spisz (1412-1795) borders on the Hungarian side; the Crimean Khanate and Ottoman frontier on the Black Sea (the Cliopatria coast of 1450-1467 is not checked); Podolia and Moldavia's frontier; the 1569 transfers inside the union (Podlachia, Volhynia, Bracław, Kyiv from the Grand Duchy to the Crown, 6 June 1569, about 170,000 km2 per the Muscovite-Lithuanian Wars page), which do not change the composite shape. (6) The dynasty also held the thrones of Hungary (1440-1444 and 1490-1526) and Bohemia (1471-1526), drawn by their own rows; Sigismund I's sister Isabella Jagiellon married John Zápolya in 1539 (Eastern Hungarian Kingdom dossier). (7) Gazetteer names needed: Oświęcim and Zator (coordinate discs are used), Sebezh, Zavoloche; Gomel resolves (place 'Gomel'), Smolensk land is covered by the region 'Smolensk'. (8) Page disagreements: Peace of Thorn 10 October (text) vs 19 October (infobox) 1466; the Union of Krewo 13-14 August 1385 (text) vs 1386 (infobox); Union of Lublin 1 July vs 4 July 1569; Lithuania's loss in 1494 (87,000 km2) is 2.4 times Cliopatria's 36,000 km2. (9) Area: the page-derived figures (1,000,000 km2 Commonwealth at its apogee; Lithuania losing 210,000 km2 as a third) are consistent with Cliopatria's 1,054,018 km2 and 815,401 km2. (10) Repair pass of 2026-10-25 after the reviewer's fail, six more pages than the budget of 9 (Gomel, Duchy of Livonia, Wild Fields, Polish-Teutonic War 1519-1521, Duchy of Oświęcim, Duchy of Zator). Starodub dropped from keyframes _1537 (now _1535), _1540, _1547, _1556, _1561, _1564 and from ledger 22-24; Gomel is the contest zone and the 1535 gain (Gomel page), cut from the keyframes of 1503-1534 and lost in March 1503 (confidence 2: the transfer to Moscow is undated on the page). Disagreement kept: the Wars page's 'Gained 20,000 km2' (1537) is larger than Gomel's disc (about 12,900 km2) and stays unexplained; Starodub was fought over in 1534-1537 but is not drawn as contested. Livonia: the 1561 gain is now the Livonian land (Vidzeme, Latgale, south-western Estonia, less the Muscovite east and the Danish coast), 225 cells; Courland and Semigallia is subtracted from the direct shape and carries the vassal tint of ledger 28; the page's 85,000 km2 is reproduced (about 57,000 plus about 29,000 km2). The Muscovite-held east is Cliopatria's Tsardom of Russia shape of 1564 (Dorpat, Narva, Fellin per the Livonian War page), applied also to 1561-1563. Added at confidence 2: Oświęcim (1457) and Zator (1494; the page has the duchy united with Poland in 1513) as gains with counterparts duchy-of-oswiecim and duchy-of-zator, which need dossiers; Cliopatria already draws both inside the realm from 1450 (a few cells), so no keyframe is cut. Polish-Teutonic War 1519-1521 added to wars (no border moved). The small unexplained Cliopatria cell changes (1468, 1482, 1497, 1502, 1516, 1519, 1540, 1547) remain unexplained; no page opened accounts for them.
